pr_title: Windows File System Unicode Fixes and correctly expand home directory in ATTACH/DBInstanceCache
pr_body:
This PR is a continuation of #5852

Fixes #5499
Fixes #6573
Fixes #6931
Supersedes #7266

###### Windows Unicode Fixes
This PR fixes unicode handling on Windows for various system calls by correctly using the `W` variant were necessary. These places are:

* `getenv` -> `_wgetenv`
* `SetCurrentDirectory` -> `SetCurrentDirectoryW`
* `GetCurrentDirectory` -> `GetCurrentDirectoryW`

This allows us to correctly get/set the working directory, as well as get the home directory of the user, even if they contain unicode characters.

In addition, for extension installation we use our own file system APIs instead of `iostream`, as [`iostream` is not unicode aware either on Windows](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/821873/how-to-open-an-stdfstream-ofstream-or-ifstream-with-a-unicode-filename).

This fixes #6573 and #6931.

###### Correctly Expand Home Directory & Normalize Absolute Paths

Similar to how we allow `~` to be used as the home directory when reading from files, we now correctly expand the home directory when opening databases (either through attach, the storage manager, or through the `DBInstanceCache`). This implements #7266 for all clients instead of only the JDBC client.

For #5499 we fix the normalization of absolute paths in the `DBInstanceCache` which caused this regression in the first place.
pr_comments: I wonder if this also fixes https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/issues/7246
I think that's unlikely as that is a data-issue, not a file system issue.

issue_context.title: [Python] Empty IOException upon installing JSON extension
issue_context.body:
### What happens?

Upon installation of JSON extension in DuckDB an empty `IOException` with neither stack trace nor error message gets thrown, making it difficult to debug it further. Here is a simplest example of the failing code:

```python
import duckdb

if __name__ == "__main__":
    # sys.setdlopenflags(os.RTLD_GLOBAL | os.RTLD_NOW)  # Running on Windows
    con = duckdb.connect()
    con.execute("INSTALL 'json';")
```

The process also fails when attempting installation from file:

```python
import duckdb

if __name__ == "__main__":
    # File lies in CWD
    duckdb.install_extension("json.duckdb_extension")
```
In both cases, all the error information returned is:
```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "c:\dev\projects\openai\debug.py", line 10, in <module>
    con.execute("INSTALL 'json';")
duckdb.IOException
```
It does not look to me like a problem finding the installation file not a syntax error in my SQL query. Otherwise the DB seems to function properly; I am able to connect, create a test table, insert data and fetch it via the `fetchdf` method. I am using release `0.7.1` but I got the same error with the `0.7.0`, `0.6.1` and `0.7.2.dev1256` versions.

### To Reproduce

1) Create a `pipenv` environment from the following `Pipenv` file:

````toml
[[source]]
url = "https://pypi.org/simple"
verify_ssl = true
name = "pypi"

[packages]
duckdb = "*"

[dev-packages]

[requires]
python_version = "3.10"
````
2) run the following code snippet:

```python
import duckdb

if __name__ == "__main__":
    con = duckdb.connect()
    con.execute("INSTALL 'json';")
```

### OS:

Windows 10

### DuckDB Version:

0.7.1

### DuckDB Client:

Python

### Full Name:

Daniel Moseguí i González

### Affiliation:

paiqo GmbH

### Have you tried this on the latest `master` branch?

- [X] I agree

### Have you tried the steps to reproduce? Do they include all relevant data and configuration? Does the issue you report still appear there?

- [X] I agree

Disclaimer: I NEVER write my name with accents or special characters in any computer system, precisely for avoiding such annoying encoding problems. This PC  and its accounts are managed by my employer 😆

Thanks for the work on tracking down this issue! I have pushed a fix in #7503. The issue was that we were not using Windows' special unicode-aware APIs in certain places, in particular the code to get the home directory, which then caused problems when the home directory contained unicode. I have tested this by making a user with unicode symbols in the name and it seems to work correctly but it would be great if you could also test that this works as expected now when `v0.8.0` hits (later this today/this week).

We should clean this up in the future - but currently the `FileSystem` class holds almost all OS-specific code. In this case as a static method it is not file-system specific but only OS-specific.

I will leave this as-is for now in light of trying to get this finished before the release, but that definitely should also be updated later on.
